The staged CAMELYON pyramid (stage0/data, q85 4:2:0, 95 % tissue) measures 70 KB median at level 0 but 103–123 KB at levels 1–4 — the magnifications pathologists spend most time at — and 4:4:4 adds +24 %, so q85–90 4:4:4 tissue tiles are ~90–150 KB; the Base Bundle measured 9.5 MB (85 tiles) and the Pinned Base ≈2.4 MB. issue: The in-flight and prefetch budgets ignore the bandwidth-delay product and therefore self-inflict the queueing they are meant to prevent, while simultaneously starving prefetch. W-4G: BDP = 25 Mbps × 45 ms ≈ 140 KB (≈2 tiles); the 24-slot cap ≈ 1.9 MB ≈ 14 BDP ≈ 600 ms of bytes committed ahead of any new request; the prefetch budget `0.5·bw_ewma·0.5 s` ≈ 780 KB ≈ 250 ms of queue in front of a tier-0 request at p50. W-BB: 3.1 MB prefetch budget vs 312 KB BDP, again ≈250 ms. `AbortController` below 30 % bytes stops the server sending more but cannot reclaim bytes already in the socket buffer and radio queue; Safari sends no priority signal (§7). So the common case 'tier-0 fires during a prefetch burst' costs ≈ the whole W-4G TTS p50 budget and ≈2.5× the W-BB p50 budget, and no §2 row models it. Conversely, the slot share (25 % of 24 = 6) and byte share cannot carry the 40–50 tier-1 wants §6 generates per frame (ring 14–24 + adjacent window 9–20 + cone ≤15), so on W-4G prefetch cannot lead the gesture and CHS ≥ 85 % has no mechanism.
fix: Pace by bytes, not slots: total in-flight ≤ ~2×BDP (bw_ewma × rtt_p50, both already tracked), prefetch ≤ ~1 BDP, tier-0 always admitted; derive the ring/window/cone set sizes per class from the byte budget and the gate they must achieve (residency at burst end) instead of fixed fractions; add a 'queueing behind own prefetch' row to §2 and a Tier-2 test: tier-0 issued while prefetch saturates the budget must see first byte within RTT + 1 BDP on the W-4G and W-BB profiles; keep h2/h3 priorities as a second line, never the first.

issue: A documented cause of jank on exactly the floor GPUs is missing from §14's 37 causes and from G12's protocol: modifying a texture that in-flight draws still reference. On tile-based deferred renderers the previous frame's draws have not executed when the next frame's `texSubImage3D` is issued; Arm's GPU Best Practices guide states the driver then either ghost-copies the whole resource (copy-on-write) or inserts a pipeline bubble, and recommends N-buffered copies of volatile resources (https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/67a62b17091bfc3e0a947695 ; https://developer.arm.com/community/arm-community-blogs/b/mobile-graphics-and-gaming-blog/posts/mali-performance-6-efficiently-updating-dynamic-resources). The plan's §9 design writes every frame into 64-layer, 64 MiB arrays that were bound by the previous frame's instanced draws; a ghost copy is a 64 MiB memcpy per upload on a 3 GB phone, a stall is a lost frame. §8's "Fencing: on WebGL2 the implicit command ordering makes a texSubImage3D issued after the previous frame's draw safe" is a correctness statement, not a performance one. The same class applies on Apple TBDR through ANGLE-Metal in Safari. S1-10/G12 measure upload cost into a texture, not into an array referenced by the previous frame's draw, so Stage 0 as specified will not detect it.
fix: Add cause #38 with its countermeasure: rotate uploads across arrays so a layer is written only into an array not drawn in the last 2–3 frames (add a `cooling` slot state; use more, smaller arrays, e.g. 16 layers = 16 MiB, so any ghost copy is cheap), or `texStorage3D` + fence-gated writes where available; make G12 measure (a) upload into an idle array and (b) upload into an array bound by the previous frame's draw, with the gate on (b); run G4/G12 on Mali-G52, Adreno 610 and A12 Safari; record per-upload GPU-side cost via the frame-time controller as the detector in production.

issue: The W-4G (and N-And) gate set is internally inconsistent. 01 §7.1, 02 NFR-P2/P7, 05 §2 and 08 §9 gate TTS p50/p95 ≤ 250/700 ms AND CHS ≥ 85 % AND state the cold destination fill as ≈650/3,000 ms. With 15 % of settles cold, the overall TTS p95 lies at the ~67th percentile of the cold-fill distribution (≈1.0–1.3 s for a p50 650 / p95 3,000 distribution), not ≤700 ms. W-BB (5 % cold, cold p50 230) and W-iPad (10 % cold, cold p50 250) do close, which is why the problem is specific to the radio classes.
fix: Choose one: (a) CHS ≥ 97 % on W-4G (not credible on 4G), (b) TTS p95 gate ≈ 1.2–1.5 s on W-4G/N-And with the p50 unchanged, or (c) split the gate into warm-settle TTS (≤250/700, measured on settles with CHS hit) plus a cold-fill distribution gate (≤650/3,000) plus a CHS floor; state the choice in 01/02/05/08 and in `gates/*.json`.

issue: The 128 MiB L0 budget in §9/§13 is undercounted and its protection (the DPR cap) is keyed to the wrong variable. The worked W-4G budget ("≈11 L* + 4 parent + 14 ring + 9 window + 21 pinned ≈ 59 of 128") uses average not worst-case tile counts (a 780×1688 px viewport spans up to 3×5 = 15 tiles) and counts only the parent, while §9's eviction never evicts `ancestor_of_visible` — the whole chain up to the Pinned Base (≈10–13 more slots on a 100k² slide at high power). Recounted at DPR 2: ≈88 slots, not 59. At DPR 3 — which applies on any unmetered link, e.g. a 3 GB phone on classroom or hospital Wi-Fi, since §4 caps DPR "on metered links" only — the set is ≈24 L* + 8 + 13 ancestors + 24 ring + 12–20 window + 21 pinned ≈ 100–110 of 128, above the 85 % eviction target before a single revisit tile. RA risk 2 ("phone memory does not close") is therefore live with the plan's own mitigation disabled in the education pillar's main configuration.
fix: Key the DPR cap to the L0 budget (choose the largest DPR for which un-evictable + working set ≤ ~60 % of slots), independent of network class; define `ancestor_of_visible` precisely (full chain vs parent-only) and recompute §9 with worst-case tile counts; add a proptest 'working set on a 128 MiB L0 at DPR 3 and DPR 2 ≤ 85 %' to the engine tests and a W-4G-on-Wi-Fi lab profile to M2.

issue: The 16-bit multichannel path has no residency or bandwidth model, yet 08 §9 M5 and 12 gate "8-channel 16-bit fluorescence meets M1/M2 gates on the same devices". 8 × R16 × 512² = 4 MiB per tile; a 20-tile viewport is 80 MiB, parents 20 MiB, and a Pinned Base of 21 tiles × 8 channels is 84 MiB — the pinned set alone does not fit the 128 MiB W-4G or comfortably the 256 MiB W-iPad budget (05 §13 lists brightfield only). Bytes per destination fill are ~20 × 2 MB zstd ≈ 40 MB (25× brightfield), ≈3.2 s on W-BB. The "8-bit windowed first paint then 16-bit at settle" (05 §8, 04 §9) has no defined source: a server-side windowed preview is either request-time transcoding (excluded by 01 §1 and the p99 ≤10 ms target) or a second pixel copy (excluded by RA §9).
fix: Add a multichannel table to 05 §13 per class (visible-channel cap, Pinned Base as a precomputed 8-bit composite derived at ingest and declared as a derived tier with provenance, bytes per fill); define the 8-bit preview tier explicitly (ingest-time derived pyramid, not request-time); restrict M5's 'same devices' to W-LAN/W-BB/N-Desk/N-iPad and state a phone policy (e.g. ≤3 visible channels, 8-bit composite only, 16-bit on settle for the centre tiles).

issue: TTS, Rendering Complete and the ≤100 ms cross-fade are defined so that the W-LAN/N-Desk TTS p50 ≤ 50 ms gate is unreachable whenever any tile lands after the last input: §4 says Rendering Complete requires "no cross-fade is in progress" and "TTS = last input → first such frame", while every tile that "replaces a magnified ancestor" fades over ≤100 ms (6 frames). §4's two landing cases are also self-contradictory: a tile landing "into a fractional-blend slot (parent already drawn at the correct weight) → no fade" cannot occur, because while the child was missing the parent was drawn at weight 1 as the magnified ancestor, not at weight f, so its weight drops abruptly when the child lands — that is a pop by the plan's own definition.
fix: Define TTS at fade start (first frame in which every visible pixel is sampled from L* or its blended parent with the fade merely finishing) and keep pop-in count as the separate metric; shorten the fade to ≤3 frames (50 ms) on a settled frame; rewrite the two landing cases as one rule: any change of drawn level at a pixel after the last input is faded, and the fade length is excluded from TTS but counted in BAT.

issue: NTF% and the "sharp at rest" invariant are undefined under the fractional-LOD blend. 08 §3.3 defines NTF% as frames "with any visible pixel sampled from a level coarser than L*"; §4's trilinear blend samples the parent (coarser than L*) at weight f = −log2 s on every rest frame with s < 1 (f = 0.74 at s = 0.6, parent magnified 1.67×). Either NTF% ≈ 100 % at rest by its own definition, or the blended parent is silently exempt and the metric is blind to the softness trilinear introduces — the exact blur a pathologist at 20–40× will report. No gate bounds at-rest blended deficit.
fix: Define resolution deficit per pixel including the blend weight (f·log2 s_parent) and gate the at-rest area-weighted value (e.g. ≤0.15 octave) alongside NTF% = 0 for unblended coarse pixels; measure trilinear vs pure-L* bilinear at s ∈ [0.5, 0.75] on the Siemens-star goldens and in a reader-study arm (gap-1 F9); consider blending only below s ≈ 0.75 (f = clamp((0.75 − s)/0.25, 0, 1)) if the study shows the softness is perceptible.

issue: The fragment-cost estimate for transients is 5–10× low and endangers G3. §11 budgets Catmull-Rom bicubic at "≈0.3–1 ms at 1080p on Mali-G52". Mali-G52 executes 2 texels/clock/core (Arm, https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/620e22c90ca305732a3a5dd0); an MC2 at ~0.85 GHz is ≈3.4 Gtexel/s peak. 1080p × 9 taps = 18.7 M fetches ≈ 5.5 ms at peak; at the G3 geometry (DPR 3, 2.96 MP) ≈ 7.8 ms at peak and realistically 10–15 ms with cache misses — plus the trilinear base pass and the 3 ms upload box inside a 16.7 ms frame. 01 §7.2 defines W− as "floor Android" (bilinear per §11) while 06 §1 defines W− as Xclipse/Firefox/WebKitGTK and puts Mali/Adreno Chrome in W+, so whether the floor phone gets bicubic is undetermined.
fix: Budget shaders by texel rate per device class in §11; make the transient kernel bilinear on W-4G and W-iPad and bicubic only on W+/N; reconcile the W− definition between 01, 02 and 06; add a G3 variant with transients active (ancestor magnification over 50 % of the viewport), not only 60 blended tiles.

issue: 02 NFR-P10 gates "decode p95 ≤ 4 ms per worker (WASM libjpeg-turbo, measured at G13)" on the floor phone, while 05 §8 estimates 9–15 ms per 512² tile on an A55 and gap-2 measured a 2.1–2.9× WASM penalty on top of note 04's 3–5 ms native low-end-ARM estimate (so 7–15 ms is the plausible band and 4 ms is not). An impossible gate in the requirements register will be waived at M2, which is the behaviour the agent-loop section says must never happen.
fix: Rewrite NFR-P10 as relative to the Stage-0 measurement (e.g. ≤1.2× the G13 p95 per worker, ratio to x86 recorded) and move the absolute number into the §2 table as [measured] after G13; keep the wall-time budget for 20 tiles across the pool as the gate that matters.

issue: "20 tiles" is a 1080p/DPR-1 laptop viewport; the sign-out persona in 01 §3 uses a 27" 4K display (44–54 L* tiles per level, note 03 §2.8) and W-LAN/N-Desk gates are evaluated on that persona. At 4K the W-LAN cold fill is decode 44 × 3 ms / 6 workers ≈ 22 ms + upload 44 MiB at a realistic 3–8 tiles/frame ≈ 90–250 ms ≈ 120–280 ms, against TTS ≤ 50/100. A slow pan at the pathologist ceiling (1 viewport / 500 ms) on 4K needs ~88 tiles/s ≈ 7 MB/s ≈ 56–80 Mbps with measured tile bytes, 3–4× the W-BB p95-low 20 Mbps, so 02 NFR-P14 ("edge pop-in during slow pans = 0 at ≤ 1 viewport/500 ms on W-LAN/W-BB") cannot hold for the remote 4K reporter.
fix: Add a viewport-geometry column (1080p/DPR1, iPad DPR2, 4K DPR1.5–2) to the §2 table and to the gate definitions; evaluate W-LAN and N-Desk on the 4K/DPR-2 workstation and W-BB on both 1080p and 4K; add a pan bandwidth row per class and set NFR-P14's W-BB clause to the bandwidth at which it is actually achievable (or to 1080p only).

issue: "Service Worker off the hot path" (04 §4.6/§4.7, 05 §7, 06 §4.1) has no mechanism. A PWA service worker with a fetch handler intercepts every fetch issued by the controlled page, including cross-origin tile-host requests, so a separate `{tile-host}` does not keep it off the path; the 50/250 ms cold start and a per-request hop land on the first zoom after idle. Chrome 123+ offers the Static Routing API (`event.addRoutes`, source 'network') to bypass the SW for URL patterns (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/service-worker-static-routing); no Safari or Firefox equivalent was found, and W-iPad is the class most exposed.
fix: Specify the mechanism: either no fetch handler in the SW at all (app shell cached via HTTP caching and the manifest), or `addRoutes` where available and a no-fetch-handler SW elsewhere; add a Tier-2 assertion on WebKit and Chromium that no tile request shows a service-worker timing span; add this as cause #39 in §14.

issue: Stage 0 cannot measure what it is chartered to measure on the dates given. 10 §8 needs the floor phone on days 2–3 (S1-07a, 2026-10-28/29) and G12/G13 by Sprint 1, the A12 iPad, Xclipse device and 240 fps camera/WALT rig before Sprint 3 (G11, 2026-11-24); 07 §2 says Stage 0 has "one week of buffer for device procurement" and WALT "by M2"; 06 §8 says "the lab is bought in M1, before the first mobile claim". The TSP T0 number (29 Oct) depends on a phone being on the bench on 28 Oct.
fix: Publish one dated procurement list in 07 and 10: floor phone + 240 fps camera before 2026-10-28; A12 iPad + Xclipse device + photodiode rig before 2026-11-24; WALT by M1; amend 06 §8 accordingly; make the T0 evidence pack state explicitly which device was measured and that REF was measured on it the same day.

issue: The golden gesture replay — "the single most important test" — is platform-dependent as specified. The shell's frame-time AIMD controller (05 §8) changes the upload budget per device every frame via `set_budget`, which changes how many uploads each `tick` emits, hence L0 slot state and the draw list on frame N. The .sgr recording captures "memory budget" once (08 §3.2), not the budget timeline, so byte-identical FrameOut across wasm/native/shells is either false or holds only when uploads are not budget-limited.
fix: Record every `set_budget`/`upload_per_frame` change with its timestamp in the .sgr and replay it; define the semantic golden on policy-level fields (TileKey, level, blend weight, request/cancel order) rather than (array, layer) slot ids; keep the slot-level diff as a per-platform snapshot, not a cross-platform assertion.

issue: Sparse vendor pyramids break the L* contract at first view and the frozen-section acceptance ignores it. SVS/SCN step 4× between native levels (04 §7 step 4: "this path is the norm"); index-in-place serving ("viewable seconds after upload") offers no level with s ∈ [0.5, 1.0] for half the zoom range until lazy synthesis (+25–120 ms server-side per tile, §4 table) has run for that region. 02 US-C2 nonetheless asserts W-BB/W-iPad TTS ≤ 100/300 ms on a slide "viewable ≤ 30 s after the scanner finishes".
fix: Define the L* policy on sparse pyramids (draw the finer native level minified up to 4× with the blend spanning two octaves, or the coarser level magnified ≤2×, and say which); synthesise the ROI's intermediate level synchronously in the frozen-section path and the ≤4096 levels at index time; add a 'first view after ingest' row to §2 and exclude it from the TTS gate or gate it separately.

issue: The moving tier (q75 4:2:0 during bursts, q90 at settle; §13 rung 2, 03 D13) is either request-time transcoding — which 01 §1 forbids ("No request-time transcoding, ever") and which cannot fit the translator's p99 ≤ 10 ms (a 9-tile decode+re-encode is ≈45–90 ms on one core) — or a second derived pyramid, which RA §9 counts as a storage cost. Its bandwidth arithmetic is also unmodelled: with refine-at-settle every level the user stops on is downloaded twice (q75 + q90 ≈ +60 % bytes), so the tier only pays on levels passed through, and the waste metric excludes it.
fix: Decide explicitly: a precomputed derived H&E moving pyramid at ingest (state the storage cost) or drop the tier; model total bytes per gesture with and without it against the Brunyé burst-amplitude distribution before implementation; include moving-tier bytes in the waste and bytes-per-gesture metrics; keep Dx mode excluded as already stated.

issue: §13's memory table counts GPU textures inconsistently and does not say which process it budgets. W-4G 'Peak RSS ≤250' includes L0 128 MiB (128 + 32 + 36 + 48 = 244); W-iPad 'Peak RSS ≤300' cannot include L0 256 MiB (256 + 64 + 36 + 64 = 420). On iOS 17+ WebGL textures live in the GPU process, not WebContent, and both are jetsam targets; G6 'RSS ≤300 MB' names neither.
fix: Budget per process (WebContent heap/JS/wasm, GPU-process texture memory) per class, name the counter each soak reads (`os_proc_available_memory`, JetsamEvent logs, `dumpsys meminfo`, Web Inspector), and make M2's '≤60 % of measured kill threshold' apply to each process separately.

issue: TTFI p95 ≤ 3.0 s on W-4G does not close at the class's own p95-low bandwidth (5 Mbps): 1.0 MB gz floor module + 0.1 MB Manifest + ≈2.4 MB measured Pinned Base = 3.5 MB ≈ 5.6 s, plus ≤0.3 s compile. The slide-open sequence (05 §5) also fetches the whole Pinned Base before any L* tile, which delays a launch-context jump to a saved high-power view.
fix: First frame on thumbnail + levels ≤1024 px (5 tiles ≈ 0.5 MB), then the rest of the Pinned Base; when the launch context lands at high power, order the L* viewport tiles before the remaining base; set the W-4G TTFI p95 from the measured bytes (≈6 s) or state the module-cached assumption explicitly.

issue: Correlated-burst loads are absent from the network profiles although two pillars depend on them: a 30-seat classroom following an instructor (12 §9 'M2 gates hold on W-4G in a 30-seat classroom profile') and a 30-viewer follow-me tumour board (01 §3). 30 clients × ≈2.5 MB per synchronised zoom ≈ 75 MB per instructor gesture ≈ 6 s on a 100 Mbps access point regardless of edge-cache hit rate; the §3.7 profiles are all single-client.
fix: Add a shared-bottleneck profile (N clients behind 100/300 Mbps, tc netem on the bridge) and a follow-me scenario to Tier 2/3; consider presenter-driven pre-push (broadcast of the presenter's prefetch list to followers) as a policy feature with its own waste accounting.

issue: "A pinch crosses s = 1.0 ≈155 ms after it starts" is the mean of a 0–300 ms distribution (the starting s is uniform in [0.5, 1.0] at 3.3 levels/s); the 10th percentile is ≈30 ms, below the W-BB first-byte + adjacent-window transfer (19 ms + 40–80 ms). Roughly a third of W-BB pinches therefore begin with a ≤1-level transient irrespective of prefetch quality, which the text presents as the exception.
fix: State the lead-time distribution rather than its mean; derive the NTF% gate from it; name hover/pointer-down prefetch (§6 item 4) as the mitigation and log its hit rate.

issue: Constants revised in one section were not propagated: 05 §8 makes the upload controller frame-time AIMD with timer queries as telemetry only, but 01 §7.1, 02 NFR-M3 and 08 §3.5 still say 'online budget from timer queries'; M0 main-thread task limit is 50 ms in 08 §9 but 8 ms in 05 §3 and 08 Stage 0; BER on W-4G is ≥70 % in 02 NFR-P8 but ≥80 % within 500 ms in 01 §7.1 and 08's reviewer note; the 1 M-object layer gate is 'on W-4G and N-iPad' in 12 but 'N-Desk and W-LAN, centroid LOD elsewhere' in 02 NFR-P15.
fix: Make `gates/*.json` the single source and generate the tables in 01/02/05/08/12 from it; reconcile the four values above to 05's and 02's definitions in the assembly pass.

issue: 04 §4.3 describes L* as s ∈ [0.5, 1.0] with "one level of hysteresis"; 05 §4 correctly notes the range is a partition (exactly one level qualifies at any k) and that the only hysteresis is the ε = 0.03 octave guard band. The wording in 04 will mislead an implementer into adding a dead band.
fix: Replace 'one level of hysteresis' in 04 with 'a partition with an ε = 0.03 octave guard band (05 §4)'.

issue: The decode and upload rows assume one 512² JPEG per tile, but SVS/Aperio (the dominant TCGA and clinical format) stores 256- or 240-px frames; 03's reviewer note makes a logical 512² TileKey = up to four vendor frames, i.e. four decodes and four sub-uploads per slot (~1.3× decode cost from per-image overhead), and the Pinned Base contiguity claim in §5 holds for the canonical DICOM only, not for in-place vendor files.
fix: Add a '4 × 256² frames' variant to G12/G13 and to the §2 decode row for tier-B passthrough slides; state that §5's 'all 21 tiles contiguous' applies after canonical write, not during index-in-place serving.

issue: §4 states the Base Bundle "halves that [worst-case blur] within one decode round (≈60–200 ms by class)"; 64 tiles at the plan's own 9–15 ms/tile (or more, see G13) across 3 workers is 190–320 ms on an A55, and 2–5 MB (measured 9.5 MB) of transfer precedes it on 4G.
fix: Recompute per class from the §8 decode figures and the measured bundle size; decode the Base Bundle lazily by ROI on phones rather than in one round.

issue: Stage 0 / M0 / T0 anchors disagree across sections, so every downstream gate date is ambiguous. §07: week 0 = 2026-10-26, Stage 0 weeks 0–3, M0 = 2026-11-20, Phase 1 starts 2026-11-16. §09 'Date anchors': T0 = 2026-11-02, Stage 0 exit 2026-11-13, M0 2026-11-30. §10 §8: three sprints 2026-10-27 → 2026-12-05 with the M0 scorecard/ADR-0013 on 2026-12-05 (week 6), and its Reviewer note 1 admits 'This is a schedule stretch'. §08 §9, §05 §15, §06 §6, §01 §1 and recommended.md §8 all still say 'Stage 0 (weeks 0–2)', and §08 §11 says 'end of Stage 0 plus M0 (≈ month 2)'. §07 claims it 'does not change any figure' yet M1 (2027-01-29) is only 7.5 weeks after §10's M0.
fix: Adopt §10's sprint calendar as canonical (it is the only one with itemised work and gates): M0 = 2026-12-05 (week 6). Either shift §07 Phase 1 to weeks 6–16 (M1 → 2027-02-19) and re-derive every later date, or keep M1 = 2027-01-29 and explicitly cut Phase 1 scope to fit 7.5 weeks. Delete the §09 'T0 = 2026-11-02' anchor and the 'weeks 0–2' wording in §01/§05/§06/§08 and recommended.md §8 (an ADR superseding the figure, per §11 A6). Add a single `docs/plan/calendar.yaml` that every section references so dates cannot drift again.

issue: The TSP milestone is scheduled against an unverified and wrong meeting date. §07 §6: 'the 106th is expected in early February 2027 [unverified], i.e. weeks 14–15, two weeks after M1' and 'Data freeze for the meeting: T1 = M1 (week 13, 2027-01-29)'. The verified facts (brief; also §11 B1) are 22–24 January 2027 = week 12, which ENDS five days before M1. §07 also says the TSP deadline 'could not be read ... and must be confirmed by the owner' when the brief gives it (Fri 30 Oct 2026, 17:00 CT, 350 words, no names, residents'/fellows' competition). §01 Reviewer note 3 still questions eligibility that the brief resolves. §11 B7 gets it right ('M1 ... presented only if its gates are green by 15 January').
fix: Rewrite §07 §6 and the T1 row of the milestone table: T1 = presentation data freeze 2027-01-15 (week 11), content = M0 scorecard (G1–G13 on real floor devices) + Tier-2 nightly trend + OSD comparator; M1 is explicitly NOT presentable. Replace the unverified sentences with the verified facts and the deadline Fri 30 Oct 2026 17:00 CT; keep the internal submit target Thu 29 Oct. Delete §01 Reviewer note 3. Make §11 Part B the single owner of TSP facts and have §07 reference it.

issue: The staffing and funding model is not the programme's actual situation, and the plan has no funding gate. §07 §2 Phase 0: '5.5 FTE: tech lead 1, Rust/graphics 2, Rust systems 1, performance/QA 1, backend 0.5 ... hired before week 0 or Stage 0 does not start' with week 0 two days away; §8: human roster under agent execution '≈4.5 FTE at Stage 0 rising to ≈7–8 by v1' yet 'the calendar is not shortened' — i.e. the schedule silently assumes agents supply the missing ~50 % of a 9–16 FTE team's work content at the reference team's calendar, which §07 itself calls 'uncalibrated'. No section names who pays the 4.5–8 FTE, the USD 8–12k device lab due before Sprint 3 (§10 'Procurement gate before this sprint'), the Mac mini/runner boxes (USD 4–5k, §08 §3.6), hosted CI (USD 1–1.6k/month, §08 §8) or agent tokens. gap-8 F8 names the realistic sources (NCI ITCR R21/U01/U24, CPRIT SEED/CFSA, philanthropy) and their cycles are quarters, not weeks.
fix: Add a §07 §8a with two explicit execution scenarios and make the choice an M0 human decision: (A) funded reference team (current plan); (B) owner-plus-agents, zero payroll, borrowed devices — state what B can reach (Stage 0 measurements on owned devices, M0 core + golden replay, desktop web alpha, TSP evidence) and what it cannot (device lab, reader study, clinical pilot, QMS, native shells). Put a 'funding secured' gate on the dependency graph before Phase 2 with the grant calendar (ITCR/CPRIT submission dates) as lead items, and a 'device lab PO issued' gate before Sprint 3. Replace 'hired before week 0' with 'tech lead and graphics/perf reviewer identified (paid or volunteer) before Sprint 2'. Record in §11 A6 the per-phase agent-token budget as a number (e.g. Stage 0 ≤ USD X) so the ledger has a target to burn against.

issue: The MVP is not minimal and Phase 1 is overloaded, so M2 (the only milestone that validates goal 1 on real devices) is at risk from scope that does not serve it. §02 tags 32 Must requirements at MVP, including FR-V7 fluorescence ≤8 ch, FR-A3 vector-tile path, FR-A4 raster overlays, FR-S3 both canonical stores, FR-S5 PHI tiers, FR-S7 desktop local files, FR-S8 DICOMweb/IIIF/DZI façades, FR-S9 conformance statement, and six education Musts (FR-E1/E2/E3/E7/E8/E12: collections, tours, region-marking items, case modules, unknown archive, authoring). §07 Phase 2 adds Tauri desktop, PyO3 wheel, OpenSlide worker, OSD TileSource, Hyperdrive launch, reader study, dashboard, device lab and WALT. §07 Phase 1 (10 weeks, or 7.5 after the M0 fix) carries both canonical stores, Cloudflare Worker AND regional binary, bundles, tokens, PHI bucket, Orthanc/dcm4chee reader CI, full policy, render-gl, telemetry, replay, 4-browser alpha, Tier-2 nightly and 24 h fuzzing. §07 §10's cut list leaves MVP scope almost untouched (only IIIF/DZI).
fix: Redefine MVP 0.5 as 'M2 + what M2 needs': web viewer (W+/W60/W−), DICOM brightfield passthrough canonical + regional translator, Manifest/bundles/tokens, npm + anywidget, launch-context contract v1 (mock-verified), GeoJSON import/export, quality record + dashboard. Move to v0.7/v0.9: OME-Zarr multichannel canonical and fluorescence, Cloudflare Worker build, Tauri desktop, PyO3 wheel, IIIF/DZI/Iris façades, OSD TileSource, OpenSlide worker, raster overlays, all FR-E* features (keep only the API freeze). In §02 re-tag those rows to v0.7/v0.9 and cap MVP Musts at ~15. In §07 Phase 1 keep only DICOM passthrough + regional binary + core + render-gl + replay + Tier-1/2 harness; defer multichannel ingest and the Worker to Phase 2.

ADR-0001…0012' accepted at gate H2 by 'PO, TL' in Sprint 1; §09 §5.1 'Apache-2.0 for the core ... (ADR-010)' and OQ-04 (legal entity) answered only by v0.9. gap-8 F6: 'Regents' Rule 90101: the Board owns software created by employees; creators cannot license it themselves; UT Austin and UT Southwestern have procedures that permit open-source release ... An Apache-2.0 release needs the campus technology-commercialisation office to approve the licence choice.' The owner is a UT resident; the repository already exists and §11 B6 drafts an abstract calling the project open-source. Publishing to npm/PyPI (M2) and the public perf dashboard (Phase 2) are distribution acts.

issue: Research note gap-8 (present in the corpus, 19:58) contradicts the regulatory assumptions baked into §02, §07, §08, §09, §11 and §12, all of which say gap-8 'does not exist'. (a) Class: §02 NFR-D6, §08 §11, §09 §3, §11 A10 'IEC 62304 Class B assumed'; gap-8 F4: 'expect Enhanced documentation and plan IEC 62304 Class C for the pixel pathway ... Use §4.3 segregation to keep the education/collaboration/research modules at Class A/B'. The ~10 % design-control overhead and the 3–4 PM (MVP) / 10–14 PM (v1) regulatory line in §07 §9 are Class-B numbers. (b) Builds: §12 §2 'The mode field ... is the one switch that separates the pillars legally'; gap-8 F3: 'an RUO build must differ from the Dx build in more than a flag: no LIS sign-out integration, no Dx-mode display gating, distinct name, distinct website claims ... Keep the education module a separate product with its own name'. §07 CLIN-1 then uses an 'RUO-labelled' build for 'frozen-section preliminary consult' — clinical use under a label that says 'Not for use in diagnostic procedures'. (c) Product code: §09 §3 'product code PSY'; gap-8: 'software-only viewers carry product code QKQ, not PSY'. (d) Timing: gap-8 §4.3 'Commission the Pre-Sub (free) in H1 2027 ... Stand up the QMS on documented, free tooling now ... Approach Hamamatsu and Leica for test files/display loaners'; §07 puts QMS at W84–104 and the design partner post-v1.

Replace the mode flag with three artefacts from one commit set — RUO/research build, education product (own name, no PHI), in-house clinical build (lab-validated labelling for CLIN-1), plus the later Dx edition — and fix the CLIN-1 row accordingly. issue: No section mentions TX-RAMP, yet it gates every UT deployment of a cloud-hosted service. Texas Government Code §2054.0593 requires institutions of higher education to contract only for cloud computing services that are TX-RAMP certified (Level 2 for confidential/regulated data such as FERPA records or PHI), with an 18-month provisional path (https://dir.texas.gov/information-security/texas-risk-and-authorization-management-program-tx-ramp/tx-ramp-eligibility ; https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/employees/information-security/tx-ramp/ ; https://www.winstead.com/Knowledge-Events/News-Alerts/401802/TX-RAMP-Requirements-for-Higher-Education). The architecture's hosting default is 'Cloudflare (first-class)' (recommended.md §3.1), the fall-2027 pilot (EDU-1, W44) launches from UT Canvas/Brightspace into that service, and CLIN-1 (W52) is at a UT site — but the 'on-prem edge binary behind Caddy/nginx' is scheduled at v0.9 (W52), AFTER EDU-1. §09 M5 covers SOC 2/BAA generically but not this Texas-specific gate.

Declare the pilot topology as UT-operated infrastructure (the Phase 1 regional binary on UT VMs + object store) so TX-RAMP does not apply, and pull the 'same binary behind Caddy/nginx on-prem' packaging from v0.9 into MVP (it is the same binary; only the packaging and docs move). If any Cloudflare/AWS path is used by a UT institution, file for TX-RAMP provisional status by M2 and add the cost. Verify applicability with UT ISO before M1 (OQ).

issue: Agent compute and reviewer time, the programme's real cost lines, have no budget anywhere. §07 §9 'External, non-labour costs are not in the table'; §09 §6 'Agent compute and review time: Unmeasured'; §11 A5 'monthly programme cap; kill switch owned by the Owner' with no figure; §11 A8 'Cost per merged change (reported, not targeted)'. issue: The two TSP fast-track schedules do not match each other or the repository. §10 S1-07a: 'First device number (days 2–3)' = 28–29 Oct, with the sprint starting 27 Oct and submission the same day the second device run completes — no time for validity checks or the claims-ledger check that §11 B3 requires. §11 B3 has device sessions Mon 26/Tue 27, 'measurement freeze 18:00 CT' Wed 28, submit Thu 29. §11 B3 also states 'the prototype's main.ts and harness do not exist at the time of writing', but the repository already holds client/src/main.ts (13.8 KB), harness/run.mjs and serve.mjs, and headless SwiftShader results from 2026-10-24 19:58 and 23:44; conversely the brief's 'currently empty apart from a README' is stale. issue: The M0 gate is defined differently in §07 and §08/§05. §07 M0 = 'Stage 0 exit: G1–G13' on floor devices; §08 §9 and §05 §15 define M0 as a separate 'renderer spike (desktop Chrome, synthetic)' gate on an Intel-iGPU laptop with 'golden replay identical native vs wasm' and translator p99, listed after Stage 0. §10 merges both into the Sprint-3 scorecard. issue: The RA/QA role is needed from Sprint 1 but staffed from week 30–39. §10 S1-11 and S1-12 name 'RA' as owner ('RA has reviewed wording'), S3-10's ADR-0013 needs 'PO, TL, RA'; §07's reference table has RA/QA = 0 until W30–52 ('RA/QA by week 39'), the agent-model roster '0.2→2.0', and §09/§11 say '0.5 FTE from v0.9'. gap-8 §4.2 Phase 0 prices exactly this: 'fractional regulatory consultant (20–40 h), $15–40 k'.

issue: The clinical pillar is built on an RUO label that the plan then uses for diagnostic work. 12 §2 puts "consultation, tumour board, QA, in-house CLIA-validated use" under mode `ruo`; FR-R3 says "every build labelled RUO until a Dx edition exists"; 07 CLIN-1 ships a "frozen-section preliminary consult ... RUO-labelled, in-house"; US-C1 ships LIS launch, `signoutRequested` events and STOW-RS write-back in the RUO MVP. Research note 11-gap-8 F3 (now in the corpus) says FDA judges RUO status on the totality of circumstances and that "an RUO build must differ from the Dx build in more than a flag: no LIS sign-out integration, no Dx-mode display gating, distinct name, distinct website claims." A product labelled "Not for use in diagnostic procedures" that issues frozen-section preliminaries and signs out cases is self-contradictory and jeopardises both the RUO channel and the later 510(k).
fix: Split the labelling into three legal bases, not one flag: (a) RUO build for research distribution — no LIS sign-out integration, no Dx gating, distinct name; (b) an in-house lab-validated tool build for the UT CLIA lab (CAP ≥60-case validation, lab's own labelling, LDT-rule enforcement discretion per gap-7/gap-8) — this is what CLIN-1 and US-C2 actually are; (c) the cleared Dx edition. Rewrite 12 §2, FR-R3, 07 CLIN-1/§7, 06 P13 and 09 §3 Phase 0/1 accordingly, and make the mode engine refuse clinical integration surfaces (HL7 write-back, signout events) in the RUO build so the boundary is machine-checked.

issue: The 512-px logical tile grid and the "byte-for-byte passthrough" promise for Aperio SVS contradict each other and the contradiction is frozen into the Manifest. Note 01 confirms SVS tiles are 240×240 (GT450 256×256); 02 §4.1 lists SVS-JPEG as Tier B lossless at MVP; 04 §7 defines Tier B as "prepends the JPEGTables segment" and asserts "the hash of every served tier-A/B tile equals the hash of the vendor tile"; 04 §5 fixes `tile: 512` in the Manifest schema and one `(object, offset, length)` per TileKey; 03 Reviewer note 3 admits this is "reconciled nowhere". A 512² tile cannot be assembled from 240² tiles without a DCT-domain re-mux (Tier C, as opentile does), so for TCGA's SVS corpus the byte-identity CI assertion, the Tier-B classification and US-R1's "bit-identical to what the viewer draws" patch export are all false as written.
fix: Decide before M1 and encode it: either (i) make tile size a per-layer Manifest field (240/256/512/1024) with the L0 atlas packing 4×256² per 512² layer (240 wastes ~78 % of a layer, so re-mux 240→512 at ingest instead), or (ii) classify SVS as Tier C (lossless re-mux) and drop the vendor-hash identity claim for it, replacing it with a decoded-pixel identity oracle against tifffile. Update FR-S2/§4.1 tiers, 04 §5 schema and §7 step 3, and run the 03 §9.2 cost measurement (4×256² vs 1×512² decode+upload on W-4G) in Stage 0.

issue: The research pillar's headline fluorescence gate is infeasible as designed. The multichannel canonical is 16-bit zstd core codecs only (recommended §3.1); note 02 measured bitshuffle+zstd at 52 % of raw, i.e. ~270 KB per 512² channel-tile (gap-5: 100–250 KB). A 20-tile viewport with 6 visible channels is ~30 MB per destination fill versus 1.6 MB for brightfield — ~2.4 s on W-BB (100 Mbps) and ~10 s on W-4G — yet M5 requires "8-channel 16-bit fluorescence meets the M1/M2 gates on the same devices" (TTS ≤100/300 ms on W-BB). FR-V7 and 05 §8 promise an "8-bit windowed first paint then 16-bit on settle" but no 8-bit tier exists anywhere in the store or translator; note 02's HTJ2K delivery variant was dropped with the move to core codecs and never replaced. No section computes a multichannel byte budget.
fix: Add a derived, never-canonical multichannel delivery tier (analogous to the brightfield moving tier): per-channel 8-bit windowed JPEG or lossy HTJ2K/AVIF-12 tiles (note 02 measured 4 % of raw for 12-bit AVIF q80), generated at ingest from the `omero` default windows and served under `enc=m`, with 16-bit zstd fetched only at settle in Dx/analysis contexts. Add a multichannel row to recommended §4.3/05 §2 (bytes per visible channel, by class), and restate the M5 gate as 'N visible channels at Q window on class X' with N and Q chosen from that budget.

issue: Wrong-slide / wrong-patient display — the number-one hazard of a clinical viewer, and one gap-8 F4 explicitly lists — is absent from every hazard list (01 §7.5: "magnified tile at rest", "wrong tile identity", "overlay misregistration"; 09 §3: "blur at ≥20×, pop-in, stale tile identity, PHI leak"). The plan correctly puts label/macro in PHI Tier 2, but never requires the clinical viewer to show the slide label and accession/part/block identifiers, nor to verify that the slides opened match the launch context. A pathologist signing out from a Hyperdrive iframe has no mandated way to confirm slide identity.
fix: Add HAZ 'wrong slide or patient displayed' with controls and REQ IDs: (1) clinical and Dx modes display the Tier-2 label image and the launch-context identifiers (accession, part, block, slide label text) by default via the `/assoc/label` token scope; (2) the shell verifies `LaunchContext.slideIds`/`studyUID` against the Manifest `sid` and DICOM UIDs before drawing and emits an `identityMismatch` event; (3) a contract test with mismatched launch/manifest pairs. Add to FR-I1/FR-R3 and to the ISO 14971 seed in 10 S1-12.

issue: Dx mode is defined as refusing "unvalidated displays" (FR-V4, FR-I10, 02 §5.1 allows Dx on W-LAN/W-BB browsers), but a browser cannot identify the physical display: no EDID, no monitor identity, Window Management API is Chromium-only and permission-gated, and a Hyperdrive iframe exposes neither. The display-QA module ("per-display ICC, test pattern, logged pass/fail") therefore reduces to user self-attestation in exactly the tier where the clinical persona lives, which cannot satisfy the 864.3700 pairing special controls gap-8 F1 describes.
fix: Restrict Dx mode to surfaces that can attest the display: the Tauri/N-Desk native shell (EDID/monitor enumeration + ICC) or a browser session whose device is MDM-managed and whose display pairing is pushed as configuration (`dx_profile.json`) by the hospital, with the attestation source recorded in the quality record. Change 02 §5.1 Tier 1 Dx column and 06 §10 accordingly; make the v0.9 native desktop window a hard prerequisite for the Dx edition rather than 'polish' (07 §10 cut #3).

issue: The Dx pixel pathway's colour step is specified three incompatible ways. recommended §5 and FR-V8 say scanner ICC → sRGB is "baked server-side for JPEG tiles"; 08 §4 tests "the server transform against a LittleCMS reference ... ΔE2000 ≤ 1.0" on served tiles; 05 §12 states baking is "impossible for byte-passthrough tiles without re-encoding them" and redefines it as a server-computed 33³ LUT applied in the shader, with untagged tiles. For the >90 % of volume that is passthrough, 08's test and 02's requirement describe a mechanism that does not exist, and the Dx pathway (a design-control artefact) has no single definition.
fix: Adopt 05 §12 as canonical: untagged passthrough tiles + versioned server-computed LUT applied in one shader; baking only for re-encoded/synthesised levels. Rewrite FR-V8, 08 §4 colour tests (test the LUT path end-to-end to ≤1 LSB and the ΔE target on the composited frame, not on served bytes), and amend recommended §5 'server-baked ICC' → 'server-computed ICC LUT'. Record the choice as an ADR because it fixes the Dx pathway.

issue: Every section states that research note `11-gap-8-fda-pathway-and-free-distribution` does not exist; it now does (written 19:58, after the sections) and it contradicts the plan in load-bearing places: the viewer product code is QKQ (13 clearances since 2020), not the PSY that 09 §3 asserts (01 flagged the conflict but 09 resolved it the wrong way); gap-8 recommends a free Pre-Sub in H1 2027 whereas the roadmap's first regulatory engagement is DX-0 at W104; gap-8 §1.4 shows a UT institution can be the manufacturer with fee waivers but "a state agency cannot indemnify (Tex. Const. art. III §49)", which collides with the "liability/indemnification terms" the Device Distribution Agreement in 03 §11/09 §5.1 relies on; gap-8 F8 supplies the qualification criteria FR-R7/FR-R8 and OQ-25 leave as placeholders. 11 B6 also counts "[17] research notes".
fix: Run a gap-8 reconciliation pass before assembly: set product code QKQ everywhere (09 §3, 01 note 1, 12 §2); schedule the Pre-Sub (five questions from gap-8 §3.5) in H1 2027 as a human gate in 07; add 'manufacturer entity cannot indemnify if UT' to OQ-04 and the agreement design; fill FR-R7/FR-R8 and OQ-25 from gap-8 F8's eligibility template; correct the note count and remove the 'does not exist' caveats.

issue: The dissemination plan rests on two different calendars. 07 §6 says the TSP meeting is "expected in early February 2027 [unverified], i.e. weeks 14–15, two weeks after M1" and sets the presentation data freeze T1 = M1 (2027-01-29); 01 §9 calls the deadline a "working" 29 Oct and eligibility unverified. The owner-verified facts (and 11 B1) are 22–24 January 2027 and a 30 Oct 17:00 CT deadline: the meeting falls in week 12–13, before M1. The January talk as planned would present data that does not yet exist.
fix: Adopt 11 B1's verified facts in 01 §9 and 07 §6; move T1 to a date ≥7 days before 22 Jan 2027 (≈ week 11, 2027-01-11); state that the presentation carries M0 (G1–G13 on named devices) plus the Tier-2 nightly trend, and that M1 figures appear only in the follow-up (TSP 2028 or a journal). Make 11 B7's option (ii) explicitly the carrier for M1/M2 evidence.

issue: All latency and upload rows assume a 20-tile destination fill (1.6 MB, 20 MiB upload), i.e. a 1080p viewport, while the primary clinical persona (01 §3) sits at a 27" 4K / ≥8 MP display and the lab (02 §5.4) includes a 4K 120 Hz desktop. Note 03 puts a 4K viewport at ~54 tiles per level: 2.7× the modelled bytes, decode and upload (54 MiB per level, 3–4 frames at the 16 MiB/frame desktop budget), and the §9 L0 arithmetic (two 64-layer arrays hold two levels of 20 tiles) does not hold at 4K. The gate viewport is never stated.
fix: Define the gate viewport per class in §15 and `gates/*.json` (W-LAN/N-Desk at 3840×2160 DPR 1 and 3280×2048; W-BB 1920×1080; phones at their DPR-2 cap), add a 4K column to §2 and §9 with recomputed bytes/upload/L0 rows, and run the W-LAN/N-Desk gates on the 4K lab display. Re-examine the 1024-px tile experiment for 4K in that light.

issue: Open-time byte budgets are understated against the plan's own measurement. 05 §5 budgets the Pinned Base at 1.5–2 MB and the Base Bundle at 2–5 MB; NFR-P12, 01 TTFI and the W-4G '700 ms' Pinned-Base figure derive from them. 11 A10 reports the Stage-0 build measured 9.50 MB for the 85 ≤4096-px tiles at q85 4:2:0, with coarse tiles heavier (105–123 kB) than base tiles, so the Pinned Base is ≈2.4 MB and the Base Bundle ≈2–4× the budget; on W-4G that is seconds, not 700 ms.
fix: Re-pin 05 §5, NFR-P12 and 01 §7.1 TTFI to per-level measured tile sizes (tissue-dense worst case and glass-weighted typical), make the Base Bundle prefetch metered-link-gated, and add 'bytes per level' to the quality record so the budget is recalibrated from field data at M1.

issue: The Manifest definition is inconsistent across sections. 04 §5 splits it into a ≤100 KB Manifest plus an edge-resident Range Index because "the arithmetic does not close" (≈0.6–0.8 MB of offsets per base level); FR-S3 and 05 §5 step 1 still define "one Manifest `TileIndex → (object, offset, length, codec, provenance)` ≤100 KB", and recommended §3.1/§5 is unamended. An agent implementing FR-S3 and one implementing 04 §5 will build different objects.
fix: Adopt 04's Manifest + Range Index split as canonical: amend recommended §3.1/§5, FR-S3, 05 §5 and 10 §2 (`stoi-manifest`) wording, and publish both JSON Schemas under `api/`.

issue: Three different M0 dates and Stage-0 durations: 07 has week 0 = 2026-10-26, Stage 0 weeks 0–3, M0 2026-11-20; 09 assumes T0 = 2026-11-02, Stage-0 exit 2026-11-13, M0 2026-11-30; 10 schedules three sprints ending 2026-12-05 with M0 at the end ("a schedule stretch"); recommended §8 says weeks 0–2; 11 B7 says ~12 weeks of work for the January presentation. A machine-checkable roadmap needs one calendar.

issue: Pillar features are assigned to different releases in different sections. HL7 status sync with prefetch-on-ready-for-review: v0.7 in 07 (W39), v0.9 in 12 §3.2/§3.3, v1 in FR-I6 and 01 §7.4. CAP-validation tooling: MVP in 12 §3.2/§3.4 ("at MVP"), v1 in FR-R1 and 07 (cl4, 2028). LTI launch: MVP in FR-E4 and 12, v0.7 in 07 §7. An integrator or education lead reading 12 would plan a 2027 go-live the roadmap does not fund.
fix: Treat 07 as release authority and 02 as requirement authority: fix each feature's release once in 02 (FR-I6, FR-R1, FR-E4) and make 12 §3.2/§4.2/§5.2 and 01 §7.4 cite those IDs instead of restating releases.

issue: S1-02 seeds the repository's ADR record with "0007 Apache-2.0 + DCO, Dx edition and enterprise edge commercial", the exact wording 09 ADR-010 proposes to replace with a no-charge regulated-release channel (and which 01 note 4, 03 note 2 and 09 note 1 all flag). 12 §2's licence row hedges with "commercial or regulated-release channel". Because agents treat ADRs as settled decisions, Sprint 1 would encode the wrong distribution model into the single source of truth.
fix: Reword 10 §6 ADR-0007 to 09's ADR-010 text (regulated-release channel at no charge; commercial terms only for OEM embedding/non-qualifying systems as an optional funding line), make 12 §2 and recommended §7 match, and mark the decision H2 for the owner at S1-02.

issue: The sign-out workflow assumes a Hyperdrive iframe (gap-7: Epic launches external web apps "usually in an iframe"), but a sign-out pathologist works with the LIS on one monitor and the slide on a dedicated diagnostic display. An iframe is confined to the Hyperdrive window; "multi-monitor placement (v0.9)" names no mechanism, and the Window Management API gap-7 cites is Chromium-only, permission-gated and unavailable inside a third-party iframe.
fix: Specify the companion-window pattern: the Hyperdrive activity hosts a thin controller iframe that opens (or hands off to) the viewer in a top-level window or the Tauri shell on the diagnostic display via the IID URL, with the two kept in sync through the launch-context token and the event bus; add it to FR-I2/FR-I10, to the Beaker contract tests and to the display-QA design, and verify with an Epic analyst (OQ-15).

issue: US-C2 promises the slide is "viewable ≤30 s after the scanner finishes level 0 of the region (index-in-place, lazy levels)" and 04 §7 calls index-in-place the basis of "view while scanning". For the TIFF family (SVS, NDPI, Philips) the IFD with tile offsets is written when the file is finalised, so a partially written vendor file has no index to read; only DICOM-output scanners deliver complete instances (per level or concatenation) incrementally.
fix: Scope the claim: 'view within seconds of file close' for TIFF-family scanners; 'view as each DICOM instance/concatenation arrives via C-STORE/STOW-RS' for DICOM-output scanners (GT 450 DX, the predicate pairing gap-8 recommends); drop 'level 0 of the region' unless a scanner API is identified (gap-7 found none). Adjust the frozen-section TAT acceptance accordingly.

issue: The education pillar's primary surface is an LTI 1.3 tool launched inside an LMS iframe, with iPad/Safari named as a target device. LTI 1.3's OIDC third-party-initiated login relies on a state/nonce cookie set in the iframe, which Safari and partitioned-cookie Chrome block — a well-known failure that 1EdTech's LTI Platform Storage (postMessage) spec exists to fix. Neither 12 §5.3, FR-E4 nor gap-6 mention platform storage or a new-window fallback, and whether `ltijs` 7.0.7 implements it is unverified.
fix: Add to FR-E4: launches must succeed with third-party cookies blocked (Safari iPad, Chrome partitioned) via LTI Platform Storage, with a same-window/new-window fallback; add a cookieless-WebKit launch to the `contract` tests against the 1EdTech reference platform; verify ltijs's platform-storage support before committing to it (or implement it in the TypeScript service).

issue: For the ML engineer, the 10⁶-polygon path only exists as a server ingest job: FR-A3 cuts vector tiles "at ingest" into a PMTiles-style sidecar, and 12 §4.3's export table makes the Translator the only cutter. A model-development loop produces new polygon sets every iteration, often locally in Jupyter; `layers.addVector({ url | buffers })` admits raw buffers but no section states the in-memory limit or a local tiler, so the research persona either round-trips every run through server ingest or hits an unspecified cliff.

issue: Brightfield image adjustment is missing from the viewing core. Pathologists routinely use brightness/contrast/gamma (and 'glass-like' presets) and every cleared QKQ viewer exposes them; FR-V7/FR-V8 define transfer functions only for fluorescence and CVD remap, so the clinical persona has no requirement, and Dx mode has no rule for logging or resetting adjustments (which the pixel-pathway determinism and audit trail need).
fix: Add FR-V14: per-view brightness/contrast/gamma as a 1-D LUT uniform (one-frame update, no refetch), presets, visible on-screen indicator when non-default, recorded in the quality record and State Document, reset-to-default on Dx-mode entry and logged in the AuditEvent; verify with `golden` and `contract`.

issue: The section identifies the real critical path and then refuses to act on it. §2.2 (iv): 'the critical path is our QMS, our evidence and a scanner partner, not FDA'; §7 totals: 'DX-1 moves earlier only if the QMS, the scanner partner's test corpora and CAP-1 move earlier ... drafting QMS procedures during v1 (W52–84) is the lever'. fix: Replace 'nothing there moves' with 'Roadmap §3 dates are the pessimistic bound; this section's target dates are:' and give targets: QMS SOP drafting W39–52 (when RA/QA 0.5 arrives and is already writing the 62304 process document), remaining SOPs W52–84, QMS operating from v1 (W84); signed scanner-corpus/loaner agreement or own-scanner plan by v0.9 (W52), Barco MDPC-8127 purchased at v0.9; Dx 1.0 release-candidate freeze at ≈W96; bench W84–104; DX-1 target W104–108 with W117 as the bound. Ask the roadmap owner to move 'design partner' from v1 to a v0.9 gate and to redraw the §5 dependency graph accordingly (and drop the false INH → K510 edge, per issue 54).

issue: The Pre-Sub is sequenced before the decision it depends on, and the single largest non-technical dependency has no task, owner or date. OQ-26 submits the Pre-Sub at ≈W40 (2027-08) while OQ-04/OQ-29 (who is the manufacturer; UT OGC position) are answered at v0.9 (W52) — the Gantt places 'Pre-Sub feedback' and 'Manufacturer model decided' on the same day (2027-10-29) with zero slack. Pre-Sub question 5 (is free distribution by a State entity 'commercial distribution' for 379j) only makes sense if a State entity is the submitter, so the sponsor identity must precede the filing. More fundamentally, 'the UT component institution ... registers as specification developer and holds the first 510(k)' (Decision 7) is a dean/president/OGC-level institutional commitment to become a device manufacturer with national free distribution and post-market duties — not a project decision — and the HeartSee precedent is a single-lab research product. The plan never schedules obtaining that commitment; RX-12 only supplies a 'default'. If the institution declines at W52, the fallback (501(c)(3) files) loses the fee exemption and sovereign immunity and needs a QMS from zero, and the Pre-Sub answers on fees become moot.
fix: Add a task 'Institutional sponsor commitment' owned by PO+LC: engagement with the candidate component institution's RA/compliance office, OGC and the department chair starts at M1 (W13) using the gap-8 §4.1 matrix and the HeartSee precedent; a signed letter of intent to act as specification developer by v0.7 (W39); a formal institutional decision (with the fallback explicitly priced) by v0.9 (W52) as a hard DX-0 gate. Ratify the default (UT institution holds; nonprofit stewards) as an ADR at M1 so the Pre-Sub is drafted and filed under that sponsor. Add RX-13 'component institution declines to be manufacturer' (L3, I5) with the 501(c)(3) fallback and its cost delta ($28,653 + $13,785/yr fees, insurance, QMS stand-up without institutional compliance infrastructure).

issue: The two most expensive validation items are scheduled before their own prerequisites and finish after the submission they are meant to support. (a) The confirmatory reader study runs W95–W125 (§4.2 item 3; Gantt d3 2028-09-04 + 30 w → 2029-04-02 = W126), but the phase table puts 'reader-study protocol IRB-approved' at the END of the W84–104 phase — the study starts ≈7 weeks before IRB approval is due, and two UT sites imply two IRBs or a reliance agreement plus data-use agreements and archival scanning on both scanners (2–4 months lead). (b) DX-1 is W117, so the study's data arrive ≥9 weeks after submission: a $150–400 k study that is 'complete or near-complete' at filing cannot be the 'cheap insurance' against FDA asking for one (RX-2) — it would reach FDA only as an Additional Information response, pausing the review clock and making the '81 FDA days' argument moot. (c) The HF summative 'on the frozen Dx edition' (§3.5) runs 2028-10-02 + 16 w and ends exactly on DX-1 (2029-01-22) — zero time for use-error root-cause analysis and the report, and the 'frozen Dx edition' does not exist until DX-1 itself. (d) The §4.2 power statement ('≈300 reads per arm ... 1,200–1,600 paired reads, so 300–400 cases is conservative') uses an unpaired, unclustered approximation; with 4 readers reading every case, reads are clustered by case and reader and the effective sample size can fall well below 1,200, so 'conservative' is unsupported and a biostatistician could double the case count and cost.
fix: Insert a milestone 'Dx 1.0 RC freeze' at ≈W96 (Class C pathway frozen at v1/W84; UI frozen at W96) that gates both the HF summative (W96–W112) and any reader study; file the IRB protocol at v1 (W84) with approval targeted W92. Make the reader study conditional: the decision to run it is taken at Pre-Sub feedback (W50); if FDA says it is needed, run it W96–W126 and set DX-1 to study report + 4 weeks (≈W132), explicitly trading 15 weeks for the claim; if not needed, cut the $150–400 k and keep DX-1 at the §7 target. Replace the power paragraph with a clustered (reader × case) calculation signed by the biostatistician, or state the case count as 'to be set by the statistical analysis plan, 300–600 cases'.

issue: The in-house clinical build demanded by existing issue 64 is missing, and the section contradicts itself about it. Issue 64's fix (three legal bases plus the cleared edition; the mode engine refuses clinical integration surfaces in the RUO build) is not reflected, so 12 §2, FR-R3, 07 CLIN-1 and this section would all be fixed to different answers.
fix: Amend Decision 3 to four artefacts from one commit set: Stoipath Viewer (RUO distribution build: no LIS write-back, no sign-out events, no Dx gate, RUO string asserted by CI), Stoipath Learn, the in-house clinical build for the validating UT lab (Dx mode capable; labelled under the lab's validated-system labelling and CLIA/CAP; the only pre-clearance build with HL7/FHIR write-back and sign-out events; distributed to no other institution), and Stoipath Dx (cleared). Fix the §7 v0.x wording, state that CLIN-1/CAP-1 use the in-house clinical build, and add a CI assertion (build-flag matrix) as the machine check. Propagate to 12 §2, 02 FR-R3/US-C1, 07 CLIN-1/§7 and 09 §3 Phase 0/1.

issue: Post-market funding is checked only after the obligations attach. §1 says a free product 'must fund' every post-market duty and §5.3 prices them at $350–700 k/yr plus $0.5–0.8 M/yr maintenance (≈$1.0–1.6 M/yr), but the DX-0 'Board decision to submit' gate (§7, roadmap §3) lists QMS audit, entity and PCCP draft — not funding — and RX-6's early warning is 'no signed dues or service revenue by DX-2', i.e. after the 510(k) is filed and the registration, MDR, 806 and §524B duties exist. The mitigation 'Dues programme launched at v1' and the §5.4 arithmetic '20 members × $50 k = $1 M/yr' assume 20 member health systems when FREE-1 delivers 2–5 sites in 2029; no hospital pays dues for a product it does not yet run. §5.4 also lists grant sources without cycle dates, although NIH/CPRIT awards lag submission by 9–12 months and the v0.x/v1 regulatory staffing ($150–300 k, then $500–900 k/yr) starts W39 (2027-07), implying applications in late 2026/early 2027 that nothing schedules (issue 50 asked the roadmap for a funding gate; this section owns the regulatory programme's funding and must supply its calendar).

Move RX-6's early warning to DX-0 − 6 months. Add a funding calendar table to §5.4: source, RFA/cycle date, amount, which §7 phase it funds, decision date (e.g. ITCR R21/U01 due dates 2027-02/06 → funds 2027-12/2028-04 for v1 RA/QA; CPRIT CFSA/SEED FY2027 cycle via the 501(c)(3) → DX-0/DX-2 operations; UT System programme budget → Stage 0–v0.9). Re-time dues to FREE-1 + 12 months with a realistic ramp (5 members in 2030, 20 in 2032) and state what funds 2029–2031 (UT System anchor + grants + philanthropy-with-cleared-product).

issue: The steward entity is load-bearing but unscheduled, and the two-entity hybrid has no allocation of regulatory roles. The 501(c)(3) must hold the trademark, sign regulated-release agreements (FREE-1, W143), carry $5 M product-liability/E&O/cyber cover (DX-2), raise philanthropy and be the 'Texas company' for CPRIT product-development awards, yet no phase row or Gantt bar creates it; gap-8 §4.1 itself estimates 6–9 months to stand up a new 501(c)(3) (IRS determination plus, for a 'UT-affiliated' body, Board of Regents approval under the affiliated-organisation rules — [unverified] lead time, counsel to confirm). §5.3 assigns FTEs but not entities: under the hybrid, who is the 807 registrant, whose complaint file (ISO 13485 §8.2.2) receives the intake the 501(c)(3)'s agreement mandates, who is the Part 803 reporter and Part 806 filer, who is the UDI labeler, who owns the §524B plan, and whether the 501(c)(3) that distributes a device it does not manufacture is a 'distributor' with its own recordkeeping duties — all undefined. Insurers will also ask why a non-manufacturer nonprofit is insuring another entity's device.
fix: Add 'Steward entity formation' to §7 and the Gantt: decision at v0.9 (with OQ-04), incorporation and IRS filing W52–60, Regents' affiliated-organisation approval and insurance binding by DX-0 (W104), trademark assignment/licence from UT by DX-2. Add a RACI table by regulation (807 registration/listing; 820/ISO 13485 complaint file, CAPA, management review; 803 MDR; 806 corrections/removals; 801/UDI labeler; §524B plan owner; agreement counterparty; insurance named insured) with the UT institution and the 501(c)(3) as columns, marked [unverified; OGC/FDA counsel], due at DX-0. Add OQ-35: can a non-manufacturer nonprofit obtain product-liability cover for a device whose 510(k) a State entity holds, and does the hybrid require the 501(c)(3) to register as a distributor/relabeler?

issue: Dx 1.0 is not minimal, and the section does not say what it runs on. §3.4 classifies browsers, WKWebView, OS and GPU drivers as Class C 'uncontrolled updates' SOUP and lists both renderers (`web-sys` WebGL2 and wgpu/naga) as 'C (Dx render path)', so the first submission would carry two renderers across the whole browser/OS matrix plus three Translator topologies — doubling the Class C verification surface (goldens on four GPU families, nightly browser matrix) for a first-time sponsor. The section never states the labelled platform set for Dx 1.0, which topology is in the first filing (the §2.4 'Deployment' PCCP category implies others come later, but which one is first is unsaid), or how a web page verifies its own 'cleared-configuration hash' (a served bundle cannot trust itself; the gate is only enforceable on a signed native installer or via server-side signed manifests). Existing issue 68's fix — Dx mode only on surfaces that can attest the display (Tauri/N-Desk native with EDID, or an MDM-managed browser with a hospital-pushed `dx_profile.json`) and the v0.9 native desktop window as a hard Dx prerequisite instead of roadmap cut #3 — is not reflected here, although it decides the Dx 1.0 platform.
fix: Add a §2.7 'Dx 1.0 scope': one platform family (recommended: the signed Tauri native desktop installer on Windows 11, wgpu/DX12 or Vulkan, EDID display identity; alternatively managed Chrome/Edge on Windows under an MDM-pushed profile), one topology (on-prem Edge Translator behind Caddy/nginx), two scanners (S360MD, GT 450 DX), two displays; hash verification by OS code-signing for the installer and by Translator-side signed manifest for served bundles. Everything else (macOS, browsers, cloud topology, air-gapped media) enters via the PCCP 'Deployment' category or letter-to-file. Align 02 §5.1 Tier-1 Dx column and 06 §10; tell the roadmap owner that cut #3 (native wgpu window) is withdrawn because it is now a Dx prerequisite.

issue: QMS procedures arrive after the records they must govern, and the QMS is audited before it has operated. §3.2 has a 'design-input baseline signed per train' and 'formal review minutes at baseline' from MVP 0.5 (W30), but the document-control and design-control SOPs that define what a valid signature, approver and review record are, are drafted W62–88 ('QMS procedures drafted', Gantt c1 2028-01-03); only the IEC 62304 process document is written W39–52. Records signed at W30 under no procedure need retrospective re-approval. 'QMS live, registered, internally audited' is a single 17-week bar (W87–104): an ISO 13485 internal audit and management review need months of operating records (complaint handling, CAPA, supplier controls, training) to audit, so a W104 audit of a W87 QMS is a paper exercise. gap-8 §4.3 item 3 (the section's basis) says 'Stand up the QMS ... now'. Missing entirely: validation of the QMS software itself (ISO 13485 §4.1.6, retained by the QMSR) — GitHub/CI, the DHF generator, the traceability-matrix generator, the evidence-archive signer and the e-signature scheme that §A10 relies on — which Tidepool had to do for Jira/Confluence and which is routinely underestimated.
fix: Split the QMS stand-up: (1) document-control, design-control and software-development (62304) SOPs drafted by agents from OpenRegulatory/qmsOS templates and approved by the regulatory consultant by M1 (W13) — cheap, and it makes every signature from W30 valid; (2) risk, usability, supplier, training, CAPA, complaint, MDR/806, release SOPs during v0.x–v1 (W39–84); (3) QMS operating from v1 (W84), first management review at W96, internal audit at DX-0 with ≥5 months of records. Add a deliverable 'QMS tool validation (ISO 13485 §4.1.6): GitHub, CI runners, DHF/traceability generators, evidence-archive signing, e-signature identity' with 2–4 PM at v1 and name it in §A10 of the autonomous-execution section.

issue: The pairing evidence depends on a lab and scanners the plan has not secured. Decision 2 pairs S360MD (NDPI) and GT 450 DX (SVS/DICOM); the RX-4 fallback is 'UT-owned scanners at the validating lab', and §4.2 wants CAP-1 to 'pilot the reader-study instrument' and serve as the IEC 62366 formative evaluation in the real environment. Nothing requires the CLIN-1/CAP-1 lab to own an S360MD or GT 450 DX in clinical service; if it scans on Philips or 3DHISTECH, CAP-1's concordance and HF data are collected on a pairing outside the Dx label and are useless for the submission, and the 300–400 reader-study cases ('scanned on S360MD and GT 450 DX, half each') have no scanner. 'Design partner' is used in §7 and the roadmap without definition; for a viewer whose pairings are to cleared scanners, the partner is a UT lab that owns them plus the vendor's test slides, not a co-development vendor. Separately, the §2.4 verification protocol 'byte-passthrough proof (frame-byte hash against vendor tiles)' cannot be run for the first-named pairing: NDPI stores restart-marker strips and `recommended.md` §3.1 tier C re-muxes them in the DCT domain, so tile bytes differ from the vendor file and only decoded-pixel identity after the lossless transform can be shown.
fix: Define 'design partner' = a UT CLIA lab with an S360MD and/or GT 450 DX in clinical service that agrees to host CLIN-1, CAP-1 and the reader study; make scanner inventory a site-selection criterion decided by M2 (W26) and confirmed at v0.9; if no UT lab has both, pick one scanner for Dx 1.0 and add the second via PCCP. Put 'signed test-slide/corpus access (vendor or own scanner) + Barco MDPC-8127 purchased or loaned' as a v0.9 gate, not a v1 early warning. Make the PCCP scanner protocol format-specific: byte identity for SVS/DICOM passthrough; decoded-pixel identity against the vendor strips (and against the G7 reference decoder) for NDPI and any re-muxed format.

issue: Steady-state cost is understated by a misread of the roadmap and by unitemised lines. §5.3 and Decision 10 take 'Engineering maintenance ... 20–30 PM/yr (Roadmap §9)', but roadmap §9's 20–30 PM is the additional platform effort for the whole post-v1-to-clearance period (W84–W143, ≈1.1 yr) and explicitly includes streaming mode and the upstream programme — it is not a per-year maintenance figure for a cleared product. Steady state must carry: quarterly Dx release trains with full regression and letter-to-file memos; the continuing RUO train; monthly browser and quarterly wgpu SOUP bumps with goldens on four GPU families and the browser/OS matrix; security fixes ≤30 days; 2–6 PM per PCCP pairing (several per year once hospitals bring their scanners); annual third-party penetration test on two topologies ($30–80 k external, not itemised); device-lab and photometry upkeep (09 §6: 0.2 FTE); eQMS at DX-0+ ($10–30 k/yr). A 30–50 PM/yr engineering figure [estimate] is more defensible, pushing the §5.4 'honest arithmetic' from ≈$1.0–1.6 M/yr to ≈$1.3–2.0 M/yr and the implied endowment higher.
fix: Replace the borrowed number with a cadence table (item, frequency, PM per event, PM/yr) split into RUO-shared platform maintenance and Dx-specific regulatory maintenance (trains, PCCP validations, labelling/UDI/GUDID updates, SOUP bumps with Class C re-verification); itemise pen test, lab upkeep and eQMS; restate §5.4 and RX-6 from the new total; ask the roadmap owner to label §9's 20–30 PM as period-total, not per-year.

issue: The section's staffing and cost figures are not propagated and the Class C uplift is unquantified. §7 v1 row staffs RA 1.0 + QA 0.5 + clinical affairs 0.5 + cyber 0.5 (2.5 FTE, '$500–900 k/yr') for W52–84, but roadmap §8 budgets RA/QA = 1.0 and pathologist 0.5 in that window and has no cybersecurity line at all, so 1.0 FTE is unfunded; roadmap §9's regulatory line (3–4 PM to MVP, 10–14 PM to v1, 30–45 PM after) is a Class-B estimate, 09 §6 still carries '$0.5–2 M, 12–24 months', and reviewer note 3 says to carry $1.5–3 M without converting it into PM so the roadmap's effort table can absorb it. Existing issue 53 asked for the regulatory line to be re-estimated at roughly 1.5–2× for Class C; reviewer note 2 answers only that 'documentation volume for the Class C crates rises'. Without PM numbers the two sections cannot be reconciled at assembly.
fix: Add a PM-denominated table to §7: per phase, RA/QA/clinical-affairs/cyber FTE-weeks, external hours, and the Class C delta (detailed-design documents and unit-level verification records for `stoi-codec`, the Dx paths of `stoi-draw`/`stoi-render(-gl)` and identity; a defensible one-off of ≈4–8 PM plus ≈1–2 PM per Dx train [estimate]); state that the $1.5–3 M excludes the engineering of regulatory product features (display-QA module, CAP tooling, FR-R7/FR-R8, registry, Dx train pipeline), which sit in roadmap §9's platform and clinical lines. Update roadmap §8 (add cyber 0.5 from W52, QA 0.5 from W52) and §9, and replace 09 §6's '$0.5–2 M' row with the §7 total.

issue: The §7 phase table is not machine-checkable, contrary to the programme context and to the section's own §3.7 discipline. issue: FREE-1 (first free deployment W143–156, 13 weeks after clearance) is realistic only for UT System hospitals, and the section does not say so. The §6.1–6.2 pipeline requires per site: eligibility review, legal review of a novel no-indemnity device agreement from a State entity plus a 501(c)(3) counterparty (hospital contracting for clinical software typically takes 3–6 months [estimate]), IT security attestation and — for any hosted option — TX-RAMP certification (existing issue 56), interface-engine work (priced as a paid service), training, and a ≥60-case CAP validation per application with ≥2-week washout before Dx-mode activation. External hospitals cannot validate the uncleared Dx edition before DX-2 (that would be distribution of an uncleared device), so for non-UT sites the realistic clearance-to-activation lead time is 6–12 months. The free tier's SLA (P1 workaround ≤5 business days, business-hours channel) also needs the qualification criteria to require a documented glass/downtime procedure, which §6.1 omits.
fix: Define FREE-1 as 2–3 UT System sites with conditional agreements signed pre-clearance under standard UT terms (RX-7 already notes this route) and CAP validation starting the week of clearance; add FREE-2 (first non-UT system) at DX-2 + 6–12 months with onboarding capacity stated (2–3 sites per quarter per onboarding engineer); add 'documented downtime/glass fallback procedure' to §6.1; note that a hosted option for Texas public institutions requires TX-RAMP and that on-prem is the default for FREE-1.

issue: External consultant effort is sized for an experienced sponsor. §7 budgets 'Pre-Sub 40–80 h; submission 100–200 h; $50–150 k' for a first-time manufacturer filing an Enhanced-documentation Class C software 510(k) with a PCCP (display class is novel), a §524B cybersecurity file, an HF summative report and an open-source, agent-authored codebase (RX-11). Even with agents drafting, consultant review of that package is commonly 200–400 h [estimate], and FDA counsel for the 'free distribution' and PCCP questions is listed in §7 'external roles' but unpriced.

issue: Registration timing is stated twice, differently: §7 CAP-1/DX-0 row has 'manufacturer entity registered' (W104), the DX-1 row has 'registration and listing' (W117), and §5.2 says 'before the first Dx distribution'. issue: The IEC 62304 boundary (§2.6, §3.4) is not a valid §4.3 segregation and cannot be enforced by the mechanism the plan has. (a) 'stoi-draw / stoi-render(-gl) in Dx mode' is placed in Class C while the same crates in Nav mode are Class B: a software item cannot be half Class C, and 10 §1's crate-layering test (the only enforcement named) works at crate granularity, not render-mode granularity. (b) stoi-sched and stoi-cache are classed B as 'navigation machinery', yet HAZ-1 ('magnified or stale tile presented as final image') is caused by exactly those items, and the Rendering Complete flag is computed from the draw list/`deficit` that stoi-draw derives from stoi-sched's L* and stoi-cache's residency (04 §3 step 6, 05 §15 quality record). A Class B item whose failure causes the Class C hazard must itself be Class C unless the Class C item independently verifies its output; no such independent check is specified. gap-8 F4 recommends segregating education/collaboration/research modules, not the engine's scheduler. The narrow boundary also underwrites RX-5's mitigation and Reviewer note 2's 'documentation volume for the Class C crates only'.
fix: Either (i) classify the whole deterministic engine core (stoi-core: camera, sched, cache, draw, codec, manifest/identity, render Dx path) as Class C and keep shells, stoi-annot display, education, research adapters, telemetry and server management at B/A, re-sizing the documentation estimate accordingly; or (ii) keep the narrow boundary but specify the independent check that makes it valid: Rendering Complete asserted only after a Class C verifier recomputes, from the camera scale and each drawn tile's self-identifying metadata (level, x, y from the decoded tile/fiducial, not from scheduler bookkeeping), that every visible pixel is at L* — and add that verifier as a REQ with a fault-injection test. In both cases make the boundary a crate boundary (split stoi-render into Nav and Dx crates if needed) so 10 §1's layering test can enforce it, and record the choice in the ADR issue #13 asks for.

issue: §2.1 asserts that for third-party AI overlays 'the algorithm's own clearance carries the rendering-fidelity obligation' and that displaying them is image management under QKQ. Cleared AI devices (e.g. Paige Prostate DEN200080 with FullFocus) are cleared with a named viewer; rendering their output in Stoipath Dx is outside the AI vendor's cleared configuration unless the vendor validates on Stoipath (09 OQ-18, open; 09 R12). The section therefore asserts a position 09 leaves open, with no rationale and no consequence for the Dx-mode overlay path (§2.6 'AI-overlay rendering with provenance' in Class B).

Add this as a Pre-Sub question (OQ-26 item 6) and a REQ with a golden test on the overlay provenance tuple's `regulatoryStatus`.

issue: Forced security updates (§3.6 'forced-update path', §5.3 recall row, §6.3 'quarterly Dx release train') conflict with the configuration-hash mechanism and with site revalidation. The Dx gate checks 'a matching configuration hash' (§2.6, §5.6); every patch changes the build hash, so each quarterly or forced release requires a new register entry, re-attestation at every site and, under CAP (revalidate on material change), a site decision about revalidation. The section never says whether the hash covers the whole build or only the frozen pixel pathway, nor who classifies a release as 'material' for the hospital.
fix: Specify a two-level identity: `pathway_hash` (stoi-codec, Dx resampler/colour, Rendering Complete, identity — the frozen Class C set) and `build_hash` (whole artefact). The Dx gate requires a registered `build_hash`; the cleared-configuration register and the site's CAP revalidation trigger key on `pathway_hash` (unchanged pathway = letter-to-file + no revalidation; changed pathway = new register entry, site notice, revalidation recommended). State that forced security updates never change `pathway_hash`. Add REQs and a CI check that a Dx-train release with a changed `pathway_hash` fails without a signed change-assessment memo.

Put REQ IDs in the HAZ table's control column and in 10 S1-12's risk-register seed.

issue: The QMS tooling decision ('the repository itself … electronic signatures recorded per §A10'; 'the agent toolchain as a qualified tool') lacks the two positions a reviewer will ask for. (a) ISO 13485 §4.1.6 requires validation of software used in the QMS (git hosting, CI, the trace generator, the e-signature mechanism) and 11 A10 says signatures are 'Part 11-style'; neither section says who validates the repository/CI as the record system, how audit trails and signature manifestations are preserved across history rewrites/squash merges, or how records are retained independent of GitHub. (b) RX-11's mitigation is a 'tool qualification record for the agent toolchain', but hosted LLMs cannot be version-pinned; 11 A6 records `model_id/model_version/prompt_template_sha` yet nothing defines what qualification means for a tool that changes under the project.

State the agent-toolchain position explicitly: agents are not qualified tools whose output is trusted; they are untrusted generators whose output is verified by qualified deterministic checks (goldens, replay, G7, trace gate), with model/prompt identity recorded for reproducibility only. Make that the RX-11 mitigation and align 11 A6/A10 wording.

fix: State 'risk register seeded at Sprint 1 (10 S1-12), formally baselined at M1' everywhere; use 07's Phase numbers in §7; name the intended-use requirement in whatever namespace #6 settles (e.g. `REQ-REG-001`); add `docs/qms/` and `docs/qms/ddp-<train>.md` to 10 §1's tree and use 10's paths in §3.1/§3.2.

issue: Decision 2 names 'Barco MDPC-8127 plus one Dell medical display' but the Dell is never identified; the only Dell in the predicate chain (Sectra K193054's MR2416, 24″ 1920×1200 ≈2.3 MP) fails the §2.4 display class (≥8 MP 27″ 4K), so the second named pairing is either undefined or inconsistent with the class the PCCP proposes. The reader study also assumes archival cases can be 'scanned on S360MD and GT 450 DX (half each)' without saying which UT lab owns both scanners (RX-4 assumes 'UT-owned scanners at the validating lab'; 09 OQ-24 asks the format mix but not scanner ownership).
fix: Name the second display (a ≥8 MP medical-grade Dell, e.g. the current 8 MP MR-series model, verified against its 510(k) pairing list) or drop to one display; add 'which cleared scanners the validating UT lab(s) own' to OQ-24/OQ-29 and to RX-4's early warning.

issue: Establishment registration is dated three ways: §5.2 'Register and list before the first Dx distribution'; §7 CAP-1/DX-0 row 'manufacturer entity registered' (W104); DX-1 row 'registration and listing' (W117). Registering at W104 starts the annual establishment fee ($13,785 unless exempt) 9–12 months before any distribution. Separately, §6.4 says 'a site that stops attesting for 30 days is contacted' while the same paragraph says air-gapped sites 'report by signed export at each update', i.e. they cannot attest for months by design.
fix: Pick one registration point (initial registration and listing within the 30 days after DX-2 clearance, before FREE-1) and use it in §5.2 and §7; add an air-gapped exception to the 30-day rule (contact if no signed export within one support-window quarter).

issue: RX-1's fallback ('if FDA declines to review a voluntary 510(k), the 501(c)(3) files as the manufacturer') silently changes Decision 7 (UT institution holds the first 510(k) and the fee exemption) into a different programme (nonprofit QMS from zero, fees payable, no sovereign immunity) with no cost or timeline, and Decision 7 cites 'precedent UTHealth/McGovern HeartSee' inside the fee-exemption clause although HeartSee's later versions were filed by Bracco commercially, so the precedent evidences only that a UT institution can hold a 510(k), not that it was fee-exempt.
fix: State the fallback's consequences (entity formation 6–9 months, QMS stand-up, fees $28,653 + $13,785/yr, insurance) and its decision point (Pre-Sub feedback at W44–50); move the HeartSee citation to the 'UT can hold a 510(k)' claim and tag the fee-exemption applicability as OQ-26(5).

issue: The TSP timeline is not reconciled with the regulatory deliverables: the regulatory strategy memo and the three intended-use statements are 'signed at M1' (2027-01-29), five days after the verified meeting (22–24 Jan 2027), so the presentation cannot show them; and the section does not say what the abstract/presentation may claim about design controls (at the 2026-10-30 deadline no REQ IDs, SBOM or risk register exist yet — S1-11/S1-12 land in Sprint 1–2). The MVP row also introduces 'traceability ≥95 %' without a source (08 §11 defines ≥90 % at M1 and 100 % for Dx).
fix: Date the strategy memo and intended-use statements before 2027-01-22 (they need no code) and list them as presentation evidence; add one sentence to §4.2's closing paragraph on what the abstract may say about regulation ('run under design controls from the first sprint' only if S1-12 is merged before the data freeze; otherwise 'designed to'); either source the 95 % MVP threshold from 08 §9 or remove it.
